title: Choking — What To Do
blurb: Telling mild from severe choking in an adult, then back blows, abdominal thrusts, 999 and CPR.
siteNotes: Who the first aiders are on each shift
Where the first aid kit and defibrillator are, and who calls 999
legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer gives adult choking steps only. Technique for babies and young children is different and is not covered; confirm the venue wants that stated or taught elsewhere.

CHECK: the trainer says to call 999 if the blockage does not clear quickly. Current Resuscitation Council UK / St John Ambulance guidance for a severe choke is to call 999 once back blows and abdominal thrusts have not worked, or earlier if someone else can call. Confirm the trainer's wording matches the first aid provider's current guidance.

cards.title: Choking — What To Do
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- tell mild choking from severe choking
- give back blows and abdominal thrusts in the right order
- know when to call 999 and start CPR

cards.title: Work out which first
cards.body: Where food and drink are served, choking can happen. Knowing what to do in those few seconds can save a life.

left.title: Mild
items: Can still cough, speak or breathe

right.title: Severe
items: May clutch their throat, going red then blue

cards.title: Let them cough
cards.body:
If the person can still cough, speak or breathe, it is mild.

Encourage them to keep coughing. It is the most effective way to shift the blockage.

> Do not slap their back at this stage.

cards.title: Five back blows first
cards.body:
If it is severe, act immediately. Lean them forward and give up to five sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.

Check after each one to see if it has cleared.

cards.title: Then abdominal thrusts
cards.body: If back blows do not work, give up to five abdominal thrusts.

items.title: Fist above the belly button
items.text: Place a fist just above it

cards.title: Alternate, and call 999
cards.body: Keep alternating five back blows and five abdominal thrusts.

items.title: Call 999
items.text: Or get someone to, if it does not clear quickly

cards.title: Get them checked
cards.body:
Even after a severe choking episode that clears, especially if abdominal thrusts were used, the person should be checked by a medical professional.

Stay calm: you knowing these steps could be the difference.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Mild: encourage coughing, no back slaps
- Severe: up to five back blows between the shoulder blades
- Then up to five abdominal thrusts; keep alternating
- Call 999 if it does not clear quickly; CPR if they collapse
- A medical check afterwards

cards.q: If someone is choking but can still cough and speak, you should:
options: Give them a drink to wash it down
cards.why: Mild choking: encourage them to keep coughing, the most effective way to shift the blockage.

cards.q: A severe choking victim may be unable to speak, cough or breathe.
cards.why: In severe choking they cannot speak, cough or breathe, and may clutch their throat and go red then blue.

cards.q: For severe choking, you first give up to five:
options: Glasses of water to clear it
Back blows between the shoulder blades
cards.why: Lean them forward and give up to five sharp back blows between the shoulder blades.

cards.q: After five back blows have not worked, what do you give next?
cards.why: If back blows do not work, give up to five abdominal thrusts.

cards.q: You should alternate five back blows and five abdominal thrusts.
cards.why: Keep alternating five back blows and five abdominal thrusts.

options: Never, unless a doctor tells you to
If it does not clear quickly or they become unresponsive
Only after the person has fully recovered
Once the thrusts have been tried twice
cards.why: Call 999, or get someone to, if the blockage does not clear quickly or the person becomes unresponsive.

cards.q: If a choking person collapses and is unresponsive, you should start CPR.
Where do you deliver back blows?
options: On the back of the neck
cards.why: Use the heel of your hand between the shoulder blades.

cards.q: After severe choking, especially if thrusts were used, the person should get a medical check.
cards.why: Even if it clears, they should be checked by a medical professional.

cards.q: The most effective thing for a MILD choke is:
cards.why: Coughing is the most effective way to shift a mild blockage.
